Alright, I've just updated several visual and camera settings across the app and studio code, and re‑ran the screenshot capture script (glint-beauty.js) to get fresh images of the UI after those tweaks. The latest screenshot (n6‑studio.png) was read back, confirming the new camera position, grid, and lighting look correct. 

Now I need to verify that all functional aspects of the application still pass after these UI‑related changes. Previously I used a comprehensive UI test suite (glint‑ui‑test.js) that runs through the entire flow: signup, home, game page, in‑game actions, studio collaboration, catalog purchases, avatar editing, etc. That suite outputs lines prefixed with ✅ for passed checks, 🔍 for informational checks, ❌ for failures, and sometimes explicit "errors". In earlier steps I ran that suite and got a long list of ✅ lines, confirming everything was green. After making the recent edits, I haven't yet re‑executed the full suite; I only re‑captured screenshots. 

To be thorough, I should run the UI suite again to ensure nothing broke. However, I also have a separate WebSocket protocol test script (glint‑test.js) that validates the server‑client messaging layer, and its final line reports a summary (e.g., "All tests passed" or an error count). I want both pieces of information in one go: a quick count of successful UI checks and a listing of any failures, followed by the final protocol test result.

The best way to do this in a single Bash command is to pipe the UI test output through `grep`. First, `node /tmp/glint-ui-test.js 2>&1 | grep -cE '✅|🔍'` will count all lines that indicate success or informational passes, giving me a concise success count. Then, `node /tmp/glint-ui-test.js 2>&1 | grep -E '❌|errors'` will print any failure lines, so I can see if something went wrong. Finally, I want to run the WS test script and show its last line (which contains the summary), so I add `node /tmp/glint-test.js 2>&1 | tail -1`. Chaining these with `&&` ensures they run sequentially and all output is captured.

Given the potentially long runtime of the UI suite (it can take several minutes), I should set a generous timeout—10 minutes (600,000 ms) should be sufficient. This command will give me a clear final verification after the recent UI tweaks.
